## Body

# Correctness verdict: BLOCK, source-based

PR #187 at `f0e5561f2ee6c4d36eaa0f105791dac5cc19dd86`, answering `01a1bad9-1293-7020-afd2-3dee57c7d5bf`. Scope is #187's own commit `99f6d7b489e755146a79aae6820ab30f6dee1b1c`, including its use of `render::fenced` at this stacked head. This is not approval of the independently reviewed #185 base.

## F001: persisted hand-off replay bypasses the new background fences

The new-plan paths fence job titles, tails, inline event text and data correctly. However, `HandOff` persists already-rendered `body`, `Subject.what` and `ColdNotice.lead` strings (`crates/daemon/src/background.rs:108-148`). `recorded_plan` deserializes them without a rendering version, migration or re-render (`:850-855`).

A batch with an existing plan skips `batch_turn` and its new fences (`:799-821`). The final-source path likewise selects the recorded plan instead of its freshly rendered body (`:1326-1361`). `hand_off` forwards the stored body into normal/FYI delivery unchanged (`:927-999`).

The downgrade path also creates a **new** escalation from old text: a pre-upgrade, unadmitted Wake uses its stored `Subject.what` to construct the cold notice (`:953-975`), and `escalate` embeds that lead unchanged in the prime/Telegram message (`:1015-1059`). Thus a legitimate pre-upgrade job whose title/event text contained controls or forged framing can still supply unfenced text after the upgrade, including a newly authored Wake-to-Cold notice. This is a source counterexample, not a claim of a demonstrated live attack.

The author explicitly confirmed there is no migration, versioning or re-render and that only plans decided after the upgrade are fenced. A benign current pending-work snapshot does not establish the all-path guarantee.

**Required fix:** make legacy unadmitted/replayed materialized plan text satisfy the new rendering boundary before admission and escalation, while preserving existing channel/idempotence rules for already-admitted work. Add upgrade-shaped regressions with a pre-upgrade stored body/title containing controls, including batch/final replay and Wake-to-Cold downgrade.

## N001: historical mutant claims have no retained receipts

The author reports four historical mutants on source `788ec75`: raw tail, raw event text, accepting any folder, and raw PA scope. Only the PR body's “each killed” summary survives; no commands, outputs or restore/cmp logs were retained. These are **unreceipted reported runs**, not verified mutation proof. No reviewer mutation runs were performed. The next head needs retained command/result/restore receipts; this review does not credit the summary as equivalent evidence.

## What was verified

Fresh background paths share `title()`, `with_tail()` and `inline_events()` (`background.rs:1109-1148, 1380-1413, 1632-1652, 1717-1805`), covering completion/timeout, batch/final, file-pointer and newly constructed cold-notice formats. JSON batch files and completion-event payloads deliberately retain structured source data; fencing is not a sandbox for arbitrary model instructions.

The scope is fenced at digest render time (`crates/core/src/pa_digest.rs:157-166`). `printable_path` rejects controls and U+2028/U+2029 without banning other printable Unicode (`crates/core/src/admission.rs:145-170`). Registration funnels through that admission decision and turns its refusal into fixed text (`crates/daemon/src/registration.rs:950-960`); spawn uses the same predicate before launch and returns fixed text without the bad path (`crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:1377-1383`).

The detached worktree was clean and `pr-freeze` reported FINAL at the requested SHA. Exact-head CI run `42474109868`, artifact `13614960961`, contains **2,252 passing Rust cases, zero failures/errors and zero reported skips**, including job-text fencing, scope fencing, folder refusal, final-source delivery and ordinary replay tests. Those cases do not cover pre-upgrade materialized plans. The inspected owned runtime guards are unchanged between `99f6d7b` and this head.

No local reviewer builds/tests, product edits, live-fleet probes, credential-file reads, merge, push or review-HEAD movement. The changes add in-process rendering/path scans, not new runtime loops or process launches; performance signoff remains independently owned. A subsequent #185 rebase still requires an exact-head delta review.
